summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for Tier 0 Tier 1 Tier 2 Strategy; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [high] Tier 0 strategy targets highest criticality applications requiring fully-automated failover during regional outages, demanding SLOs above 99.99% with RTO in seconds and RPO approaching zero. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/deployment-paradigms.md, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/design-guides/disaster-recovery

[high] Tier 2 strategy targets lowest criticality applications that can be down for 24 hours without significant revenue impact, with an RTO above 8 hours (Atlas deployment paradigms); Azure's comparable Business Operational tier targets SLOs around 99.9% with RTO and RPO in hours, while SLOs below 99.9% and RTO of hours to days describe Azure's Tier 3 (Administrative). Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/deployment-paradigms.md, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/design-guides/disaster-recovery

[low] Tier 2 (Business Operational) optimizes costs by using cold standby setups and pay-as-you-go options like spot instances and consumption pricing. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/design-guides/disaster-recovery

[low] Tier 3 (Administrative) prioritizes cost savings by relying on backup and archival storage with longer recovery windows. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/design-guides/disaster-recovery
